You are investigating a documentation question for the Zimmermann SFCC PWA Kit project. The question: "For the Front End, particularly the PWA Kit, what does it use to get product information — SCAPI or OCAPI?"

Your job is ONLY the Confluence side. Use the mcp-atlassian Confluence MCP tools. You will need to load them first with ToolSearch, e.g.:
ToolSearch query: "select:mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search,mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page,mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_space_page_tree,mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page_children"

The relevant Confluence space key is "SFCC" (site: zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net).

Do the following:
1. Run several CQL/text searches across Confluence for: "SCAPI", "OCAPI", "Shopper API", "Open Commerce API", "commerce-sdk", "commerce-sdk-isomorphic", "Shopper Products", "SLAS", "API version", "product API", "hooks OCAPI", "cartridge". Use both `confluence_search` with simple text queries and CQL like `space = SFCC AND text ~ "OCAPI"`.
2. For each page that meaningfully mentions either API, fetch the page content and extract the EXACT relevant quotes, the page title, page ID, URL, and last-modified date.
3. Pay particular attention to: architecture/TSD pages, integration design pages, API/middleware pages, environment topology pages, and any spike write-ups.
4. Note explicitly any page that CONTRADICTS another, and note stale pages (old last-modified dates).

Report back:
- A list of every Confluence page that references SCAPI or OCAPI, with page ID, title, URL, last modified date, and the exact quoted lines.
- A clear verdict on what Confluence claims the PWA/front-end uses for PRODUCT data specifically (vs other data like orders, customers, content).
- Any contradictions or ambiguity between pages.
- Explicitly state if you found NOTHING on a given search — do not invent or infer. Only report what you actually read.

Be exhaustive. Do not summarise away the specifics — I need quotes and page IDs.

# Confluence audit: SCAPI vs OCAPI for PWA Kit product data

## Verdict

**Confluence says SCAPI — specifically the Shopper Products and Shopper Search APIs, reached through the MRT proxy, consumed via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`.** Exactly one page states this as a *verified* finding rather than an assumption; a second states it as architecture. Everything else in the space that mentions OCAPI is about a different concern (backend cartridge CI/CD, inbound catalogue import, BM admin config, or third-party cartridge hooks).

**The catch:** the two most recently modified pages in the space (both created 12 Aug 2026) treat this as *still open*, and one of them contains a hook-name defect that makes its "SCAPI vs OCAPI" options analysis self-contradictory. Detail in Contradictions below.

---

## Primary evidence (product data, front end)

### 349437965 — "SFCC MRT API Capabilities: Spike Findings (SFCC-122)" — version 19
URL: https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/349437965
Author: Angelo Navarro, Squad-A / FED Lead. Status: "Approved by @Manikandan Ramachandran (Deactivated)". Verified against dev sandbox `bkzk-002`, 23-24 Jul 2026. Changelog entry dated 27 Jul 2026.

This is the definitive source. Exact quotes:

> "**What "MRT API" means here.** Managed Runtime is the PWA Kit hosting/proxy layer. Product, category, and pricing data are served by **SCAPI (Salesforce Commerce API, the Shopper APIs)**, reached through the MRT proxy (`/mobify/proxy/api`)."

> "The storefront consumes SFCC through the MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/api`, base host `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` (Dev: shortCode `qmyt7hks`, org `f_ecom_bkzk_002`, site `ZimmermannAU`). Authentication is **SLAS private-client** (guest and registered tokens; the client secret is held server-side)."

API inventory table, verbatim rows:

> "| Shopper Products | `/product/shopper-products/v1/*` | Product detail (master/variant, images), **price** (`priceRanges` per pricebook), and the **category tree** (`getCategory`) | GET | SLAS |"
> "| Shopper Search | `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category product listing (`cgid` refinement), keyword search, faceting, sort | GET | SLAS |"
> "| Shopper Login (SLAS) | `/shopper/auth/v1/*` (`oauth2` token and JWKS) | Guest and registered auth; the enabler for every read above | GET, POST | n/a |"

> "**Payload conventions.** The storefront pulls related data in one call with `expand` (e.g. `expand=prices,promotions,variations,images`) and `perPricebook=true` for pricebook-aware pricing."

The single most load-bearing line on OCAPI in the whole space:

> "**Out of scope** (other problems, documented elsewhere): cart and checkout (Shopper Baskets, Shopper Orders), account and wishlist (Shopper Customers), personalization (Shopper Context, Einstein), **OCAPI (configured but not called by app code)**, MuleSoft direct reads, and the Managed Runtime Admin API."

> "**Conclusion:** SCAPI serves product, category, pricing, and promotional pricing in dev today, and the storefront renders them with **no code change**. Consumption is not the blocker."

Permanent-vs-workaround table:

> "| SCAPI-via-MRT for product/category/pricing consumption | **Permanent** (the storefront's supported model; no code change needed) |"
> "| SLAS private-client auth via MRT | **Permanent** |"
> "| OCAPI via MRT | Configured fallback; currently unused |"

### 256835585 — "Technical Solution Design – PWA" — version 11
URL: https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585
Page header states "Last updated 2026-07-16."

Data-flow legend:

> "* **PWA → SFCC:** all commerce data (catalogue, cart, pricing, customer, orders) via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`."

Frontend stack table (§3.1):

> "| Server / async state | TanStack Query via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` | All SFCC data fetching |"

Integration map (§7.2) — the only OCAPI mention on the entire page:

> "| **SFCC (SCAPI)** | Storefront, catalogue, basket, customer, orders, BM config, domestic checkout | Browser (Shopper API via `commerce-sdk-react`) + MRT (token refresh, **OCAPI residue**) | Browser-direct + MRT-mediated | SLAS client ID public in bundle; SLAS client secret on MRT for the public-client PKCE flow; refresh tokens set as `httpOnly` cookies by the Node layer, never visible to JS |"

§8.1.1, on rendering:

> "| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | **SSR shell + CSR data** — server renders the layout, header, footer, and skeleton; `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hydrates personalised data (basket lines, customer profile, orders) client-side after hydration |"

---

## Contradictions and ambiguity

### 1. The two newest pages reopen the question (created 12 Aug 2026 — today)

**406913046 — "TSD-SFCC-268 – PDP Maximum Purchase Quantity – BM Config" — version 1, Draft, unsigned.**
URL: https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/406913046

This page lists the answer as an *unconfirmed assumption*:

> "| PWA Kit consumes product data via SCAPI Shopper Products API (`/shopper/products/v1/products/{id}`). | **If OCAPI is used instead**, the extension point changes from a SCAPI hook to an OCAPI `afterGET` hook — see Section 3 for both options. |"

> "| **Option B** — OCAPI Hook (`dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` on OCAPI endpoint) | + Same resolution logic as Option A ... | - Only valid if PWA Kit is consuming OCAPI Shop API, not SCAPI — **PWA Kit default is SCAPI** - Mixing OCAPI and SCAPI introduces dual maintenance overhead | **Yes — if OCAPI confirmed** |"

Decision Record row:

> "| 12 Aug 2026 | [Name, Technical Architect] | OCAPI hook implementation documented as Option B for teams not yet on SCAPI | Functional parity with Option A; included to cover both API layers |"

**This is a real documentation defect, not just caution.** Option A is labelled "SCAPI Hook" but its hook name is `dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` — identical to Option B's. The two options are therefore mechanically indistinguishable, and the page's own risk table admits it:

> "| Hook name differs between SCAPI versions — hook does not fire | Low | Confirm hook name (`dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET`) against current SFCC version documentation before registration. | Developer |"

Same page also routes SCAPI config through the OCAPI settings screen:

> "The custom attribute `c_maxOrderQuantity` must be added to the SCAPI endpoint configuration (**Open Commerce API Settings** in BM) ... Confirm under **Administration → Site Development → Open Commerce API Settings → Shop API**."

Two further inconsistencies on this page worth noting to whoever owns it: it references `app/hooks/useProduct.js` and `cartridge/hooks/product.js` (`.js`, against the repo's TypeScript-only rule for `overrides/`), and it lists the storefront scope as "AU, UK, US Dom, US Intl, EU, ME" — six, where every other doc says eight.

**407666693 — "TSD: VIC Exclusive Product Visibility" (TSD-SFCC-303) — version 2, Draft.**
URL: https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/407666693

> "| Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + SCAPI (headless). No alternative platform is in scope. |"

But the implementation table names an OCAPI hook under a SCAPI label, and a PDP controller that does not exist in a headless PWA:

> "| SCAPI Search Hook (`dw.ocapi.shop.product.search`) | Inject refinement filter on `isVICExclusive` based on session customer group membership. | New |"
> "| PDP Controller (Product-Show or equivalent) | Add guard: if product `isVICExclusive = true` and customer group ≠ VIC, return 404. | Modified |"

`Product-Show` is an SFRA controller route. In a headless PWA Kit storefront there is no such controller to guard.

### 2. "OCAPI is deprecated" vs OCAPI still in active use

**312508418 — "TSD: Catalogue Sync — Product, Price & Inventory (MuleSoft → SFCC)" — version 10** states twice:

> "**API Note:** OCAPI is deprecated. All job trigger and status poll calls use the **SCAPI Jobs Admin API** ... Authentication uses **Account Manager OAuth2 (AmOAuth2)** — not OCAPI Client ID/Secret."
> "The `sfcc-site-archive-import` system job is triggered by MuleSoft via the **SCAPI Jobs Admin API**. OCAPI is deprecated and must not be used for new integrations."

**315490342 — "TSD: Catalogue Sync — SCAPI Admin API Design (Alternative Pattern)" — version 3** repeats it:

> "**API Note:** OCAPI is deprecated. All SFCC Admin API calls use **SCAPI Admin APIs** authenticated via **Account Manager OAuth2 (AmOAuth2)** — client credentials grant."
> "⚠️ **No SCAPI Admin API exists for writing pricebook entries.** ... OCAPI is deprecated and must not be used for new integrations."

Against that:

**292061208 — "TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration" — version 10** still specifies OCAPI for the inbound feed:

> "| Import method | MuleSoft → SFCC **OCAPI Data API** (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) or SFCC SFTP + import job |"
> "| 1 | Confirm MuleSoft delivery mechanism to SFCC — **OCAPI Data API vs SFTP + import job**; confirm trigger (event-driven vs scheduled batch) | Integration Lead / MuleSoft team | Open |"

**264896514 — "SFCC Build and Deployment Process – Headless Architecture" — version 22** uses OCAPI throughout the backend CI/CD:

> "* Cartridge-based custom logic exposed through **SCAPI / OCAPI**"
> "│ ├── plugin\_zim\_scapi/ # Zimmermann — **SCAPI / OCAPI hook overrides**"
> "| `SFCC_CLIENT_ID` | Secret | **OCAPI / WebDAV OAuth client ID** |"
> "| **OCAPI Data API** | Code version management, job execution | Client credentials OAuth: `SFCC_CLIENT_ID`, `SFCC_CLIENT_SECRET` |"
> "| sfcc-ci (npm) | **CLI wrapper for OCAPI operations** | Included as a dev dependency |"
> "| `instance:import` (**OCAPI** job) | OAuth client credentials | `<SFCC_INSTANCE>` |"

**309657601 — "Business Manager Configuration Management" — version 3** confirms OCAPI is provisioned at sandbox creation, which is exactly what SFCC-122 meant by "configured but not called by app code":

> "| **Automated first-time config** | Instance-level settings (WebDAV, **OCAPI**) are applied once at sandbox creation via the `zimmermann-sfcc-admin` GitHub Action — never manually |"
